title: Pyridine N-oxidation
conditions: H₂O₂ / AcOH; peracetic acid formed in situ
description: The terminal peroxide oxygen is transferred to pyridine nitrogen. O–O cleavage and proton transfer give the N-oxide and acetic acid.

title: Nitration at C4
conditions: HNO₃ / H₂SO₄; electrophile represented as NO₂⁺
description: Net C–N bond formation at C4, followed by loss of the ring proton. The 2D panel shows the sigma-complex stage; acid/base partners are condensed.

title: Methoxylation by substitution
description: Methoxide replaces the C4 nitro group. This net bond-change animation condenses the addition–elimination sequence shown in the reference.

title: Boekelheide rearrangement
description: Net conversion of the C2 methyl group into CH₂OAc, with removal of the N-oxide. O-acylation, deprotonation and the formal rearrangement are condensed; this is not a unique computed pathway.

title: Hydrolysis to the alcohol
description: Hydroxide replaces the pyridylmethoxy group at the acetyl carbonyl. Proton transfer gives the alcohol; acetate is the coproduct. The tetrahedral stage is in the reference.

title: Alcohol to chloromethyl pyridine
description: Net replacement of OH by chlorine; SO₂ and HCl are formed. Activation through the chlorosulfite is shown in the 2D panel. The reacting carbon is CH₂, not a stereocentre.

title: Benzimidazole ring formation
conditions: CS₂ / KOH in aqueous ethanol; work-up
description: Two nitrogens join the CS₂ carbon and one sulfur leaves as H₂S in this neutral-form bookkeeping model. The displayed 2D panel condenses proton transfer, cyclisation and tautomerism. The source preparation uses the diamine hydrochloride.

title: S-alkylation joins the branches
description: The S-nucleophile approaches the CH₂ carbon as chloride leaves. Benzimidazole tautomerisation gives the depicted J. NaOH generates the nucleophile and neutralises G·HCl; those preparatory proton transfers are omitted.

title: Asymmetric oxidation to esomeprazole
conditions: Ti(OiPr)₄ / (S,S)-DET; controlled H₂O, toluene; then CHP / DIPEA
description: Terminal peroxide oxygen is transferred to sulfur, giving the major S sulfoxide and cumyl alcohol. Catalyst preparation precedes oxidation. This schematic outcome does not depict an established titanium catalytic cycle.
